verdict.rationale: Google Authenticator does have its own export feature: docs describe creating a QR code on the old device and scanning it on a new one, and community reports confirm it can export all saved codes into one QR code. However, that QR is documented only for re-import into Google Authenticator, it bundles multiple accounts that other TOTP apps might not read, and users say a simple text export is very hard to get, so the open-format, leave-anytime goal is only glancingly met. Missing for 10: open, human-readable export format (e.g., plain otpauth URIs or a text/JSON file), documented compatibility with other authenticator apps, and first-party docs describing migration away from the app.

support.subject: As a power user, I can export all my TOTP secrets in an open, readable format and leave for another app whenever I choose — no lock-in

citations.quote: On your old device, create a QR code... On your new device, tap Scan QR code
If you use Google Authenticator without a Google Account, you can still manually transfer your codes to another device.
Google Authenticator has a feature to allow export of all saved codes into one QR code for re-import into Google Authenticator running on another device.
